issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking specific performance must prove readiness and willingness to perform the essential terms of the contract, assessed from the pleadings and the parties’ conduct and circumstances.

A purchaser’s failure to take timely steps, pay a substantial part of the consideration, and act promptly after the stipulated performance period may establish lack of readiness and willingness and defeat a claim for specific performance.
A court may enhance the consideration to balance equities when granting specific performance only where the purchaser has satisfied the statutory requirements for that relief.
The applicability of the pre-2018 version of Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act to agreements made before its amendment remains unresolved.
